one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company catalyst falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30: Q3 FY27 results are due around early December (Q2 was reported Sep 1; the fiscal quarter ends Oct 31). The two big events have already happened: the CEO exit to Meta (8-K Sep 28; stock -18% from $410 to $335) and the Investor Day (Sep 29), which raised long-term targets and reaffirmed Q3/FY27 guidance. Short-horizon considerations: (a) partial reversal after a sharp news-driven drop is already under way ($335 -> $356); (b) the board added $1.0B of buyback authorization on Sep 25 ($1.35B remaining), a modest support for the price; (c) the permanent-CEO search leaves headline risk both ways (a strong external hire is upside; key-executive departures are downside); (d) software/AI sector beta. Net: roughly symmetric around $356 with a slight upward tilt (median about $358), at a monthly vol of about 16.5%, a little below the 71%/3.5 = 20% rule because the realized figure is inflated by two event gaps (earnings -13.5% on Sep 2, CEO exit -18% on Sep 28) and no comparable event is due in the window.

fair_value.method: Average of forward P/E and EV/NTM-sales set at the end of Sep-2027. P/E: NTM non-GAAP EPS of about $10.2 (a blend of FY28 at $8.6 and FY29 at $11.0) x 38 = $388. EV/sales: NTM revenue of about $4.12B x 7.5 = $30.9B EV, plus about $2.7B net cash, divided by 83M shares = $405. Blended fair value $395 (rounded).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Oct-27 to Sep-28) non-GAAP EPS of about $10.2 x 38 = $388. FY28 revenue $3.64B (+20% on the $3.03B FY27 high-end guide), 22.5% non-GAAP operating margin, net income about 0.9x operating income, 86M diluted shares -> $8.6. FY29 revenue $4.37B (+20%), 24% margin -> $11.0.

inputs_detail.derivation: Investor Day raised the long-term (about 3-year) target to 20%+ total revenue growth and mid-20s Atlas growth. The FY27 guide implies 21-23%. Q3 is guided at 20-21% and management flags Q4 as the toughest comparison, so I use the low end of the new target.
FY27 guide is about 21% at the high end. The long-term target is 100-200 bps of expansion per year on average, and I use about 150 bps.
FY27 guide: non-GAAP operating income $626M midpoint vs EPS $6.48 x ~86M fully diluted shares = ~$557M, so a ratio of about 0.89. Interest income on $2.4B of cash is offset by non-GAAP tax.

Q2 fully diluted weighted shares were 85.8M and basic shares outstanding 80.56M on Aug 28, 2026. Buybacks ($200M in 1H at an average $300.10; $1.35B authorization remaining) roughly offset SBC dilution.

Today $356 against NTM EPS of about $7.5 (FY27 H2 guide run-rate into FY28) is about 47x. By Sep-2027 growth slows to about 20% and SBC is still about 20% of revenue, so I compress the multiple toward about 38x. That is about 1.9x PEG on about 20% EPS growth, in line with where the stock traded after the CEO shock.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Sep-2027 of about $4.12B (1/3 x FY28 $3.64B + 2/3 x FY29 $4.37B) x 7.5 = $30.9B EV, plus about $2.7B cash and no debt, divided by 83M shares = $405.

inputs_detail.derivation: FCF conversion is at the upper end of 80-100% of about $700M of non-GAAP operating income, so roughly $0.75B of FCF over 12 months. I assume about $0.45B of buybacks against the $1.35B remaining authorization.
$356 x ~82M shares = $29.2B market cap, less $2.4B cash = $26.8B EV, divided by about $3.3B NTM revenue.

In Sep-2027 the business should grow about 20% at a 23-24% margin (Rule of 40 around 44), with net ARR expansion of 122% and a 17% rise in $100K+ customers. A slight de-rating from about 8.1x today reflects slower growth.
Basic 80.6M plus in-the-money awards, net of buybacks.

bear.story: Atlas slows below 20% as Q4/FY28 consumption normalizes, the CEO search drags on or other executives leave, AI data-layer spend goes to hyperscalers/Postgres, and the multiple compresses to about 5x NTM sales (about $230).

base.story: Revenue grows about 20-21% with Atlas in the mid-20s. Margins expand about 150 bps a year, a credible permanent CEO is named within 6-9 months, and the stock re-rates toward about 38x NTM EPS / 7.5x sales.

bull.story: AI workloads (Voyage, vector search, Agent Engine, Atlas Infinite) keep Atlas at 27%+, total growth holds in the mid-20s, and a strong CEO hire restores the premium. The buyback shrinks the share count, and 10x sales / 50x EPS gives about $540.

thesis_break_reason: Around $240 (about 5x NTM sales, below the Sep-2025 levels and near the 52-week low of $215.68), the stock would be pricing Atlas growth falling toward the teens and/or a leadership vacuum. That would mean the durable-growth thesis behind the new 20%+ long-term target has broken, not just event volatility, since the business ran 30% growth with 122% net ARR expansion as of Q2.

Durability of Atlas growth after the Q4 FY27 comparison; consumption revenue has little visibility beyond the current quarter
Whether AI workloads become material revenue (AI natives are still low single digits of Atlas revenue) or go to Postgres/hyperscaler alternatives

reasoning: Primary documents show a fundamentally strong business at a lower price. The Q2 FY27 8-K/10-Q show revenue of $771.8M (+30%), Atlas +29%, EA & other +36%, a 24% non-GAAP operating margin, FCF of $137.6M, no debt, $2.41B of cash, and RPO +91%. The FY27 guide was raised to $2.99-3.03B (21-23%), with non-GAAP EPS of $6.39-6.58 and GAAP profitability. The stock still fell 13.5% on the print because the Q3 guide ($756-761M) steps down sequentially and Q4 is flagged as the toughest comparison. The Sep 28 8-K CEO exit (Desai to Meta after less than a year; Ittycheria back as interim) cut another 18%. The Sep 29 Investor Day deck (8-K Ex. 99.1) nonetheless raised long-term targets to 20%+ total growth, mid-20s Atlas and 10%+ EA ARR growth over about 3 years, with 100-200 bps of margin expansion a year, 80-100% FCF conversion and a path to $5B+ revenue. It also disclosed that AI natives are still only low single digits of Atlas revenue, growing 165%. A footnote-level fact from the 8.01 item: the board added $1.0B of buyback authority on Sep 25 ($1.35B remaining; 1H buybacks averaged $300.10). A 10-Q detail: 80.56M basic shares, 85.8M fully diluted. Valuation of $388 (P/E) and $405 (EV/sales) blends to about $395, 11% above $356. The sell-side is higher (mean target about $457 across 41 analysts; DA Davidson/Stifel $465, Guggenheim $560), and I treat that as evidence, not the anchor. The scenarios (bear $230/25%, base $395/50%, bull $540/25%) give a mean of about $390. I shade the median to about $375 to reflect leadership-transition drag and the Q4 comparison risk. For the ladder I used a lognormal with median about $375 and sigma about 0.50, below the 71% realized vol because two one-off event gaps inflated it, but above a typical large-cap. That gives P(>=356) of about 0.54. Research was limited to about 10 queries; Twelve Data analyst endpoints were unavailable on this plan.
